intent: Add projectWeeklyHours to Project and enforce per-user per-week validation (backend only)
instructions: Per new.xlsx: Project Weekly hours (integer, max 999, optional). One timesheet = one user, one project, one week. When SET: enforce week total <= projectWeeklyHours. When NOT SET (null): use default 40. Backend only. 1) Add projectWeeklyHours to Project entity (integer, nullable, <= 999). Migration and run. 2) In timesheet entry validation: if project.projectWeeklyHours is set, sum hours for that project in that week for that user and reject if sum would exceed projectWeeklyHours. 3) Return clear 400 error when cap exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: Project has projectWeeklyHours (integer, nullable, max 999)
Timesheet entry validation enforces project weekly cap when set
API returns clear error when weekly project hours exceeded
When not set (null): weekly limit is 40

intent: Project Weekly hours field + use project limit in TimesheetEditor validation/display (requires project-weekly-hours-cap-backend)
instructions: Requires task project-weekly-hours-cap-backend completed. Frontend must adhere to project limits so validation and UI match backend. 1) Add optional Project Weekly hours input to Project create/edit form (number, max 999). 2) TimesheetEditor: when loading a timesheet, ensure project is available (timesheet.project or fetch by timesheet.projectId). API must return project.projectWeeklyHours. 3) In TimesheetEditor use weeklyLimit = project?.projectWeeklyHours ?? 40 (project takes precedence). Use it for: validation (highlight/weekOver when grandTotal > weeklyLimit), display (e.g. grandTotal/weeklyLimit not hardcoded 40), submit disable. 4) When save fails with backend weekly-cap error, show that error. No hardcoded 40 for this timesheet's project when project has projectWeeklyHours set.
acceptance_criteria: Project form has optional Project Weekly hours (max 999)
TimesheetEditor uses project.projectWeeklyHours ?? 40 for weekly validation and display
Weekly cap display and validation match backend (project limit when set, else 40)
Backend error on weekly cap exceeded is shown to user

intent: Add maxHoursPerDay to Project and use in daily validation (backend only)
instructions: Per new.xlsx: Max number of hour in one day configurable per project (replace hardcoded 8). Backend only. 1) Add maxHoursPerDay to Project entity (integer, default 8, e.g. 1–24). Migration and run. 2) One timesheet = one project. When project.maxHoursPerDay SET: day total <= it. When NOT SET (null): use 8. In createEntry, updateEntry, validateEntriesForSubmit load project and use dailyLimit = project.maxHoursPerDay ?? 8.
acceptance_criteria: Project has maxHoursPerDay (integer, default 8)
Timesheet daily limit uses project maxHoursPerDay when set
When not set (null): daily limit is 8

intent: Max hours per day on Project form + use project limit in TimesheetEditor and Dashboard (requires project-max-hours-per-day-backend)
instructions: Requires task project-max-hours-per-day-backend completed. Frontend must adhere to project limits so validation and UI match backend. 1) Add Max hours per day to Project create/edit form (default 8, integer). 2) TimesheetEditor: ensure project is available when loading timesheet (timesheet.project or fetch). Use dailyLimit = project?.maxHoursPerDay ?? 8 (project takes precedence). Use it for: day validation (highlight days over dailyLimit, not hardcoded 8), labels (e.g. Max X per day), submit disable. 3) Dashboard quick entry: when project is selected, use that project's maxHoursPerDay ?? 8 for 'max X h today' and input max so user cannot enter more than project allows. 4) When save fails with backend daily-cap error, show it. No hardcoded 8 for this project when project has maxHoursPerDay set.
acceptance_criteria: Project form has Max hours per day (default 8)
TimesheetEditor uses project.maxHoursPerDay ?? 8 for daily validation and display
Dashboard quick entry uses selected project's maxHoursPerDay ?? 8
Daily cap display and validation match backend (project limit when set, else 8)
Backend error on daily cap exceeded is shown to user

intent: Enforce re-request policy: editing a PENDING timesheet sets status back to DRAFT; APPROVED timesheets are immutable (backend only)
instructions: 1) Implement server-side rule: when an owner edits a timesheet with status = 'pending', allow changes but set status = 'draft', clear approved_by/approved_at, record audit event timesheet_re_requested, and notify approvers. 2) When attempting to edit a timesheet with status = 'approved', return 403 with clear message. 3) Add tests covering pending->edit->draft transition and approved edit rejection. 4) Ensure operations are transactional and use optimistic locking to prevent lost updates.
acceptance_criteria: Editing a pending timesheet succeeds and status becomes draft
Approved timesheet edit attempts return 403
Audit event recorded for re-request and approver notified
Tests cover the behavior

intent: Make frontend UX match re-request policy: warn user when editing PENDING timesheet and block edits for APPROVED (frontend only)

acceptance_criteria: Pending-timesheet edit shows re-request warning
Approved-timesheet edit UI is disabled with clear CTA
Backend 403 is handled and message shown
